$comment: What a bus log shows of a payload, as every bus log must show it. With SEMIONT_BUS_LOG set, a Semiont SDK or service writes one line for each frame it sends or receives, and the last thing on a line is the frame's payload. No line holds a credential. One rides the bus: the token a resource is cloned by, which the registry's payloads name `token` wherever they carry it (`yield:clone-resource-requested` and `yield:clone-create`, which a client sends, and the `response` of `yield:clone-token-generated`, which it receives). THE RULE reads a name and no channel: the value of a member named `token` is shown as the text `[withheld]`, wherever in a payload the member is (in the payload itself, in an object within it at any depth, in an object inside an array) and whatever its value is (text, a number, null, an object, an array: the whole value is replaced, and nothing within it is read). The name is matched whole and as it is written: `maxTokens`, `tokens` and `Token` are other names, and are shown. Everything else is shown as it is: every other member, an array's items in their order, a value that happens to be the word. A frame's payload is an object, and so is every case's. A log that can be given a payload that is not one reads an array by the same rule and shows anything else as it is, and holds that in its own tests. A case is a `payload` and what is `shown` of it. How a log writes what it shows (as JSON, as a console's rendering of an object) is its own, so a runner compares values and never text. A case that is a channel's own payload names the `channel`, and its `payload` is one the registry's schema for that channel admits. TypeScript runs this in packages/core (bus-log-cases.test.ts) against busLog, which the Node services and the Browser write with. Rust runs it in packages/sdk-rust (src/bus_log.rs) against bus_log, which the Rust transport and the gateway write with. Python runs it in packages/sdk-python (tests/test_bus_log.py) against its own bus log, and holds each case that names a channel to that channel's payload type. A bus log in another language runs it too. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: yield:clone-resource-requested, as a client sends it: the request is its token
yield:clone-create, as the gateway has it: the token is withheld, and what it rides with is shown, the gateway's stamp included
yield:clone-token-generated, as a client receives it: the token is a member of the reply's response
a token deep in a payload is withheld, and the members beside it at each depth are shown
a token in an object inside an array is withheld, in each object that has one, and the array keeps its order
an array inside an array is read too
a token that is a number is withheld, and is shown as the same text
a token that is null is withheld: the name decides, not the value
a token that is true or false is withheld
a token that is the empty text is withheld
a token that is an object is withheld whole: nothing within it is read or shown
a token that is an array is withheld whole
a name that only contains the word is another name, and is shown: the counts of a model's tokens the protocol carries, a plural, another case
a value that is the word, or the text a token is shown as, is no member of the name
a payload with no token is shown as it is: text of any script, numbers, null, and what is empty
the empty payload is shown as it is
